title: J.X: Or if they leave that sense for an obscurer one unknown to Pontificii — Jesuit-like equivocation charge (Dorsche p.183)
pass_a_gloss: Or while they withdraw from this sense and follow an obscurer one, certainly unknown to most pontifical doctors and Estates of the Empire at that time — handed down by Dorsche at the cited place page 183 at the end — they are found guilty of a matter of equivocation not unlike Jesuit ones, which those men elsewhere not rarely, though quite wrongly, are accustomed to pin on the Reformed.
pass_b_english: Or when they leave that sense and take an obscurer one — one most papal doctors and Imperial Estates then did not know — Dorsche at the place cited (p. 183, end) still leaves them open to a charge of equivocation not unlike Jesuit practice.
Papal writers elsewhere often pin that charge on the Reformed, though quite wrongly.
source_text: Vel dum ab hoc sensu recedunt, & obscuriorem, certe Pontificiis Doctoribus & Statibus Imperii plerisque isto tempore ignotum, sequuntur, a Dorscheo cit. loc. pag. 183. in fine traditum, aequivocationis, Jesuiticis haud absimilis, rei inveniantur, ab illis alias haud raro, etsi satis perperam, Reformatis impingi solitae.

lemmas.note: non-papal reading of early AC wording

lemmas.gloss: accustomed to be pinned on the Reformed

choices.why: keeps the Jesuit-comparison sting without inventing a soft gloss

notes: Hexades Annotationum jx densify section 134; Pass A!=B; locked PDF 212-213; Dorsche p.183.
